This video was made possible thanks to everyone on the Simple History Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/simplehistory

In 1979, when the Soviet Union invaded Afghanistan, soldiers faced rotten logistics and bad rations. To get food, they began trading ammunition with Afghan merchants—but it was risky, because the Mujahideen weren’t a formal army and could funnel the “trade” back into the fight. The Soviets had to keep the ammo from being obviously fake, so they tried a covert workaround: boil the bullets for 4 to 5 hours to destroy the primer, but not heat the cartridge enough to explode. The hope was simple—normal-looking ammunition that would misfire, jam, or cost the enemy a firefight. What other Cold War survival tactics should we cover next?
